summary: This bill expands the types of entities from which participants in the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) can purchase fresh, nutritious, unprepared foods using cash-value benefits and coupons, and establishes a Technical Assistance Center to support farmers and farmers' markets in accepting these benefits.

scores.thoughts: The bill mandates the establishment of a Technical Assistance Center and requires the Secretary to issue regulations and maintain a public website, all of which would incur administrative costs, thus increasing government spending. However, the bill does not specify new funding allocations, focusing more on administrative changes to existing programs.

The bill expands the types of entities from which WIC participants can purchase fresh foods using their benefits and streamlines the process for farmers to accept these benefits. This makes it easier for beneficiaries to access nutritious food, thereby expanding the social safety net.
